titulo: Accusative pronouns and negation (kein and nicht): Accusative pronouns

aula.titulo: Accusative pronouns and negation (kein and nicht)
aula.objetivo: Replace the direct object with pronouns (ihn, sie, es, mich, dich…), negate nouns with «kein» and everything else with «nicht», and answer negative questions with «doch».

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you negate sentences with nicht or kein without hesitating, know where nicht goes, and answer negative questions with doch or nein.

blocos.contexto: Jonas wants to go out with Camila, but she's busy.

linhas.ru: — Hallo Camila! Hast du heute Abend Zeit?
linhas.pt: — Hi, Camila! Do you have time tonight?
linhas.audio: Hallo Camila! Hast du heute Abend Zeit?

linhas.ru: — Leider nicht. Ich habe keine Zeit, ich lerne noch.
linhas.pt: — Unfortunately not. I don't have time, I'm still studying.
linhas.audio: Leider nicht. Ich habe keine Zeit, ich lerne noch.

linhas.ru: — Morgen habe ich Zeit. Aber ich spiele nicht gut Fußball.
linhas.pt: — Tomorrow I have time. But I don't play soccer well.
linhas.audio: Morgen habe ich Zeit. Aber ich spiele nicht gut Fußball.

linhas.ru: — Kein Problem! Wir spielen nicht Fußball, wir trinken Tee.
linhas.pt: — No problem! We won't play soccer, we'll have tea.
linhas.audio: Kein Problem! Wir spielen nicht Fußball, wir trinken Tee.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a second trap: English uses "not … any" where German uses one word: "I don't have any time" = «Ich habe keine Zeit», "I don't have anything" = «Ich habe nichts». No "do", no "not … any". STEP 2: is there an ein (or no article) in the positive sentence? Swap it for kein. Otherwise, use nicht.
blocos.comparacao: English negates with "not" and usually needs "do": "I don't live in Berlin. I don't have a car. I don't have time." German has no "do" at all, and it splits the work between two words: «nicht» for verbs, places and adjectives, and «kein» — literally "no", as in "I have no car" — for nouns.

tabela.regra: negates the verb or the place: nicht
negates a noun with ein or no article: kein

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the DIRECT OBJECT is what receives the action: in «Ich sehe den Mann», the one I see is «den Mann». STEP 2: to avoid repeating the noun, we replace the object with a pronoun: «Ich sehe den Mann» → «Ich sehe ihn» (I see him). STEP 3: for things, the pronoun follows the noun's GENDER, where English always says "it": «der Tisch» → «ihn»; «die Lampe» → «sie»; «das Buch» → «es»; «die Bücher» → «sie». STEP 4: English already does this with people: I → me, he → him, we → us. German does the same: «ich» → «mich», «du» → «dich», «er» → «ihn», «wir» → «uns», «ihr» → «euch». STEP 5: careful with «sie» (her, them) and «Sie» (you, formal): context and the capital letter tell you which is which.
blocos.comparacao: English object pronouns are the closest match in the whole lesson: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. German has the same idea — mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie — with one twist: a thing gets «ihn» or «sie» according to its gender, never automatically "it".

exemplos.ru: Wo ist der Schlüssel? Ich suche ihn.
exemplos.pt: Where's the key? I'm looking for it.

exemplos.ru: Wo ist die Tasche? Ich finde sie nicht.
exemplos.pt: Where's the bag? I can't find it.

exemplos.ru: Das Buch ist gut. Ich lese es gern.
exemplos.pt: The book is good. I like reading it.

erros.motivo: A direct object takes the accusative — like he → him.

blocos.enunciado: Replace objects with pronouns out loud: «Ich sehe den Mann → Ich sehe ihn», with 5 sentences of your own.
Write the accusative of «der Mann», «die Frau», «das Kind» and «die Kinder», with the definite article.
